title: fix(core)!: org_user_ids holds every member of an organization with more than 1,000 members
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9P46GvEyAUWWadkKbQCv3hz)_

Fixes #29281

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
Metadata-protocol: none
Skills-docs: none — no skill or doc teaches the 1,000 bound or a size limit for the organization peer list; `content/docs/permissions/rls.mdx` describes `current_user.org_user_ids` as "User ids in the user's org", which this makes true, and the bind-parameter ceiling is the interim's, removed by the relational predicate (#29360).

The claim declared `no` for an interim that reads the membership to completion. The seat's ruling (6577690137 on #29281) reads the refusal past the bound-parameter limit as a narrowing, so this PR carries `!` and the full dogfood battery.

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：成员超过 1,000 人的组织里，普通成员在人员选择器搜索和按 id 读取用户时，重新能看到每一位同组织成员；组织外的人依旧看不到。
- 为什么改：同组织成员名单只读了前 1,000 条成员记录，之后的成员被静默隐藏（搜索为空、按 id 读返回 404），而且隐藏的是谁由随机 id 决定。
- 风险与回滚：不足 1,000 人的组织读取次数和可见范围完全不变；更大的组织每个请求多读一次完整成员名单（实测 2 万人约 45 毫秒）。属于破坏性变更的只有超过数据库绑定参数上限的超大组织（SQLite 实测 3.2 万可用、4 万报错）：其成员读用户时会明确报错，而不再返回残缺名单。回滚即撤销本 PR。
- 先看：packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts 中的 readOrganizationMembersToCompletion，以及第 5 步那一处“读满即续读”的判断。
- 两分钟验证：运行 pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run src/sys-user-org-members-past-first-read.test.ts，在真实 SQLite 上用 1,001 名成员验证搜索、按 id 读取和组织外成员不可见。
- 需要你做的：无，席位落地。

## What changes

`sys_user`'s organization-members row scope is `id in current_user.org_user_ids`: the object's `defaultRowScope` and `member_default`'s `sys_user_org_members`. The authorization resolver builds that list per request from one `sys_member` read for the active organization, bounded at 1,000 rows. The bound used to be the list. In an organization with more members, everyone past the 1,000th `sys_member.id` was left out with no signal: a people picker's search found nothing, and a read by id answered `404`.

This PR is the server-only interim the card's ruling asks for. It makes no spec change and changes no metadata.

- **The first read is unchanged.** It has the same filter, the same 1,000 bound and the same leg, so an organization under the bound issues the same single read it always did and gets the same list.
- **A first read that comes back at its bound is now a first page, not the membership.** This is the same reading `countPositionHolders` gives its own reads. §5 then calls `readOrganizationMembersToCompletion` (`packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.ts`). It is a keyset read of the active organization's `sys_member` rows: ordered by `id`, `id > last` per page, 10,000 rows per page, columns `id` and `user_id` only. It starts over from the first id, because the first read asked for no order and its 1,000 rows need not be the lowest ids.
- **Loud, never short.** A page that fails to read throws the existing `AuthzStoreUnavailableError` (`503`). So do a page that repeats an id an earlier page returned (a driver that ignored the cursor) and a full page whose rows carry no id. None of them ever answers a shorter list.
- **Said once.** One `console.warn` per organization per engine names the organization, its member count and the cost: every request in that organization reads its whole membership, and each `sys_user` read binds one parameter per member. It is a `warn` and not an `error` under AGENTS.md's degradation rule, because nothing is lost: the list is complete.
- `tryFind` takes an optional `orderBy`. Changeset: `@objectstack/core` patch, with a **BREAKING** banner and an ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`).
- **The narrowing.** In an organization whose membership passes the backend's bound-parameter limit, every `sys_user` read by its members now fails loudly at the driver (`500`) where it used to answer a list missing everyone past the 1,000th member. That is the only accept-set change; below the limit, nobody gains or loses visibility of anyone.

### Who sees whom

| Organization size | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| under 1,000 members | every member, from one read | the same: one read, the same list (pinned) |
| exactly 1,000 | every member | the same members, and nothing logged; one extra read that comes back short, because a first read at its bound cannot tell 1,000 from more (pinned) |
| over 1,000 | the first 1,000 by `sys_member.id`, with the rest silently missing | every member plus the caller |
| anyone outside the organization | invisible | invisible (pinned and ablated) |

Every completion page filters `organization_id = <active org>`, and the cursor is added to that filter, never in place of it. I found no path where the old bound or the new read could add someone who is not a member. This is a visibility bug that hid rows.

### Options weighed (driver-sql over better-sqlite3 in process, median of three, on a shared box)

| Option | Per-request cost measured | Visible set | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| A. Read to completion only when the first read is at its bound (chosen) | 0 extra reads under 1,000 members. Completion read: 1,001 members 1 read, 2.9 ms; 5,000: 1 read, 9.1 ms; 20,000: 3 reads, 44.5 ms; 40,000: 5 reads, 100 ms | exact | chosen |
| B. Refuse loudly in the resolver when the first read is at its bound | 0 extra reads; every request by every member of an organization over 1,000 members fails | narrows to nothing | rejected: changes who sees whom |
| C. Log only and keep the truncated list | 0 | still wrong | rejected by the ruling |
| D. Option A with the first read's page shape (1,000 rows, every column) | 20,000 members: 21 reads, 219 ms; 40,000: 41 reads, 485 ms | exact | rejected: about 5× the cost of A's page |

Every request pays the downstream `sys_user` read with the full list:

| Members | `sys_user` search | read by id | bound parameters |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1,001 | 8.8 ms | 4.9 ms | 1,007 |
| 20,000 | 57.4 ms | 39.5 ms | |
| 32,000 | 83 ms | 58.9 ms | 32,006 |
| 40,000 | refused: `too many SQL variables` (`500`) | | |

The truncated 1,000-id list cost about 6 to 8 ms.

**Does the RLS compiler already have a relational form? No.** ADR-0139's `ReadableIds` semi-join leaf is engine-internal and cannot be authored from a scope. It projects the parent's `id`, not `sys_member.user_id`, and its inner filter is the caller's read scope, not `organization_id = <tenant>`. `rls.zod.ts` §7.3.1 states that subquery-shaped needs are pre-resolved. Replacing the list therefore needs an ADR and the spec lane. The design notes are in the card's os-dev-report, and no ADR file is drafted here.

## Why

The card's ruling is that the visible set must stay exactly the same: every member, and nobody else. On `main` an ordinary member of an organization with 1,001 members could not find the member whose `sys_member.id` sorts 1,001st, by search or by id. The ruling also says the pre-resolved list is to be replaced by a relational predicate, which is an ADR and spec-lane change. This PR is the interim the card asks for in the meantime: it keeps the set exact up to the backend's bind-parameter limit, fails loudly past it, and never shrinks the scope silently.

## Tests

- `packages/core/src/security/resolve-authz-context.org-members-past-first-read.test.ts` (new, 8 tests). It uses a double that honours equality, `$gt`, `orderBy` and `limit`, and answers an unordered read in insertion order, which is not id order.
  - 1,005 members: the exact set, with no other organization's members.
  - 20,007 members: the first read is byte-identical, then the three exact completion reads with their cursors.
  - 999 members: one read, the same set, and no warning.
  - Exactly 1,000 members: the same set, one completion read, and no warning.
  - The warning is said once per organization and engine, and names the organization and the count.
  - Loud failures: a page that fails to read, a full page without ids, and a cursor that does not advance.
- `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/sys-user-org-members-past-first-read.test.ts` (new, 4 tests). It runs a real `ObjectQL` over a real `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3), the real identity objects, the real `SecurityPlugin` falling back to the shipped `member_default`, and a principal from `resolveUserAuthzGrants`.
  - 1,001 members: the member whose `sys_member.id` sorts 1,001st is found by search and by id, and the full list is exactly the organization.
  - ⛔ A member of another organization stays invisible by search and by id.
  - 999 members: exactly one membership read and exactly the members.
  - The warning appears once and names the count.
- **Red first, on `main` `a19759ac`.** The core file was 5 failed and 1 passed at the time; the id-less and exactly-1,000 tests were added later and were shown red by ablation. The real-driver file was 3 failed and 1 passed: the 1,001-member test and the warning test failed on the defect, and the outsider pin passed on `main` as it should. The third failure was the under-bound test, whose read counter then also matched another plugin's `sys_member` read; it was narrowed to the organization read afterwards. That test pins unchanged behaviour, so it is meant to pass on `main`.
- **Ablations: each forbidden behaviour was put back with `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, ran red, and was restored to an empty `git diff HEAD`.** Core's `dist` was rebuilt for the real-driver leg and checked with `ablation-dist-preflight.mjs`.
  - The completion read drops its `organization_id` filter: core 3 red; the real-driver file 3 red, including `expected [...] to not include 'usr_outsider'`.
  - The cursor guard answers instead of throwing: the non-advancing-cursor test is red.
  - A failing page is swallowed: the failing-page test is red.
  - The completion read always runs: the 999 pin is red, with 2 reads.
  - The warning is said every time: the once test is red.
  - The id-less full page answers: that test is red with `expected false to be true`.
  - A membership of exactly 1,000 is logged: the exactly-1,000 test is red with `expected "warn" to not be called at all`.
- **Forced test edits** (`read-limits-truncate` is the one batch-equivalence fixture whose fellow-org read comes back at its bound, with 1,006 rows):
  - `resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.golden.json`: `grants.org_user_ids` gains the six members the bound cut (`peer_0999` to `peer_1004`), and `queries` gains the completion read. No other golden moved.
  - `resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.test.ts`: a fifth "recorded move" paragraph in the header. `BATCHED_LEGS['read-limits-truncate']` goes from 2 to 3, because the completion read is a leg of its own. The wave-1 filter excludes that read, which exists only because wave 1 came back at its bound.
  - `__tests__/resolve-authz-context.batch-equivalence.testkit.ts`: a comment only. The 1,000 bound is still pinned by the recorded `queries`, and the 200 bound by `accessible_org_ids`.

## Acceptance notes

- **Organizations past the backend's bound-parameter limit.** Every `sys_user` read in such an organization now fails loudly at the driver (`500`) where it used to answer a silently short `200`. On SQLite that limit was crossed between 32,000 and 40,000 members; Postgres's wire protocol caps a statement at 65,535 parameters. The seat ruled this a narrowing (6577690137), hence the `!` and the `(narrowing)` arm. The relational predicate (#29360) removes the ceiling.
- **`warn`, not `error`.** The card's example named an `error` line. `warn` follows AGENTS.md's degradation rule, which reserves `error` for silent loss, and here nothing is lost. The seat ruled `warn` (6577690137), and the 10,000-row page of `id` and `user_id` too.
- **Not measured on Postgres or MongoDB.** There is no Postgres server in the container, and the `mongod` download answers 403. The completion read uses only `where` equality, `$gt`, `orderBy` and `limit`.
- **Same family, not touched here.** The seat filed the capped `sys_member` reads in plugin-sharing and plugin-approvals as #29362. Also noted in the report:
  - Every `rlsMembership` key has the same pre-resolved, bound-per-request shape.
  - Other readers take `org_user_ids` as a value: audit mention-recipient gate, explain engine, the engine's run-as seeding, hook wrappers and the current-user endpoints. The design report lists them.

- [x] 1. Schemas start as Zod; `packages/spec` holds no runtime logic. (`packages/spec` is not touched.)
